title: SpinZero findings.json
description: The one output contract every SpinZero review producer emits: the free in-app deterministic checks (confidence 'Unvalidated'), the paid review engine, and any future CLI/CI surface. Consumers ingest it through a single path (findings -> review comments).

engine_version.description: Version of the producer that emitted this document (rule pack / prompt pack).

pipeline.description: Which review produced this. 'bom-rules' = free local deterministic checks; 'bom-detailed' = the paid LLM pipeline.

profile.description: End-application profile the rules were configured with.

run_health.description: Stages that did not fully run. Only non-clean stages appear, so a non-empty array means the result is incomplete and says why. Consumers should SHOW this: a validation stage killed by a provider error otherwise reaches the engineer as unexplained low-confidence findings.

severity.description: Two levels, deliberately. 'Important' = act before this design ships; 'Observation' = worth knowing, not a blocker. How SURE the reviewer is lives in `confidence`, not here — that split is why the old five-level scale (which mixed 'Question' into severity) is gone.

confidence.description: 'High' = verified against a datasheet, distributor record or KB entry; 'Low' = plausible but unverified, so the engineer must confirm it; 'Unvalidated' = a raw deterministic-rule hit that no validation pass has looked at — what the free tier emits.

id.description: Document-local id (B01, B02 …). Not stable across runs — use `fingerprint` for identity.

rule_id.description: Deterministic rule that produced this; null for judgment findings.

fingerprint.description: blake3(rule_id | anchor set | normalized predicate), truncated. The dedupe key: a re-run updates the existing comment instead of re-filing, and a fingerprint that disappears auto-resolves its comment.

type.description: 'bom_row' anchors to reference designators; 'bom' is a document-level finding with no single row.

stage.description: Stage id, as used in the producer's progress events.

status.description: 'degraded' = the stage ran but covered less than it should; 'failed' = it produced nothing.

detail.description: One sentence naming the real cause — a provider error, a cost cap, a timeout.
